slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop feeling awkward on
a first date (and actually enjoy it)
Pick a place you already know. Your favourite bar, a café you like, a walk you've done a hundred times. Feeling at home in the place lets you focus on her instead of the menu.
Plan something to do, not just somewhere to sit. A market, a gallery, mini golf. Doing something side by side takes the pressure off and gives you both something to talk about.
Admit you're a little nervous. "Honestly, I was a bit nervous about tonight." Saying it out loud breaks the tension instantly, and most of the time she'll admit she was too.
Order what you actually want. Don't overthink the menu to look cool. "I'm getting the burger, no regrets." Being easygoing about small things makes the whole evening lighter.
Ask about what she's looking forward to. A trip, a project, a concert next month. Talking about plans is lighter than talking about the past, and it shows you what excites her.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll always have a funny fact or story ready, and silences stop feeling like a problem.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. You'll always have a story ready, and silences stop feeling scary.

slides.texte_overlay: Send a short message after. "Had a really good time tonight, get home safe." No essay, no games, no waiting three days. Simple and honest is always the most attractive move.
